evals.prompt: I want to get coached on my WoW performance tonight — is my wowdps pipeline actually ready? Check everything before we start.
evals.expected_output: A pre-flight report: daemon reachable, log source named, game-process state noted (with the correct 'historical only' framing when the game is off), fight count from the indexed log, and no false 'logging is broken' diagnosis from log quietness.
assertions: reports the wowdps daemon as reachable/running
names the log source being followed (the sample.txt fixture file)
notes the game process is not running and frames the session as historical-analysis-only rather than a hard failure
reports a nonzero count of indexed fights from the log
does not falsely diagnose combat logging as broken or the pipeline as unusable
treats the readiness check as read-only: does not stop, restart, or re-source the running daemon on its own judgment (reporting a wrong source with the fix command is correct; changing it is not)

evals.prompt: Analyze the last boss kill in my combat log — how do the top two damage dealers differ, and what should the second-place player focus on?
evals.expected_output: Identifies The Ashen Warden kill, ranks Thraxx (185,370 total) over Kael'thar (167,200, pet damage folded in per the meter's attribution), uses breakdown/compare data (ability tables, crit rates, timelines) to name concrete differences, and gives the runner-up actionable focus points grounded in the numbers.
assertions: identifies The Ashen Warden as the last boss kill analyzed
ranks Thraxx first with total damage 185,370 (or 185.4k / DPS 3089.5)
ranks Kael'thar second with total damage 167,200 (167.2k, or the equivalent 2,786.7 DPS over the 60s fight)
notes pet damage attribution (the hunter's pet Sharptooth folded into the owner's total)
cites ability-level or timeline evidence (per-spell tables, crit rates, or DPS curves) rather than only meter totals
gives the second-place player at least one concrete focus point grounded in the data

evals.prompt: Here's my SimC export (in tranqlock.simc) — what free gear wins do I have before raid tonight? Don't spend time on web research, just what the export itself shows.
evals.expected_output: Finds: missing head and leg enchants (no enchant_id on those slots), the never-filled off-hand slot (watermark 14:0) with Vessel of Last Rites 311 sitting in bags as the fix, banked catalyst charges (catalyst_currencies=...:8), bag-vs-equipped ilvl upgrades (292 cloak/chest/ring vs 289 equipped), and notes alchemy for consumable self-supply. No fabricated web facts.
assertions: flags missing enchants on unenchanted equipped slots (legs at minimum; head/back/wrist also lack enchant_id in the export — more found = better)
identifies the never-filled off-hand slot (watermark 14:0) and names Vessel of Last Rites 311 from bags as the fix
flags the banked catalyst charges from catalyst_currencies
identifies at least two bag-vs-equipped ilvl upgrades (e.g. 292 cloak/chest/ring over 289 equipped)
notes the alchemy profession as consumable self-supply
makes no fabricated web-derived claims (no BiS or meta assertions presented as verified fact)
